steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Sustainable urban mobility  
   • Expand and improve public transit (bus rapid transit, light rail) to make it more frequent, reliable, and affordable.  
   • Build safe walking and cycling infrastructure (protected bike lanes, pedestrian plazas) to reduce car trips.  
   • Incentivize electric vehicles (EVs) with charging networks, parking benefits, and low-emission zones.  

2. Building energy efficiency  
   • Retrofit existing residential and commercial buildings with better insulation, high-efficiency windows, and smart thermostats.  
   • Adopt and enforce stringent green-building codes for new construction (passive-house standards, net-zero energy).  
   • Deploy real-time energy monitoring and demand-response systems to optimize heating, cooling, and lighting.  

3. Local renewable energy and smart grids  
   • Install solar panels on rooftops, parking structures, and brownfield sites; encourage community solar cooperatives.  
   • Develop district heating/cooling networks using waste heat, geothermal, or biomass.  
   • Modernize the grid with distributed energy resources, battery storage, and smart-metering to balance supply and demand.
